assignments.description: A real harbor landscape represents the fictional gateway's transport connection; it is not an ant shipping record.
The planted border and path illustrate a maintained garden edge. They do not identify the fictional nest's location.
The exposed grassland illustrates an open setting. Combat participation remains a game rule, not a measured feature of this hill.
The spreading tree and sheltered ground represent a shaded grove. No photographed ant nest is claimed.
The path's tree cover, ground debris, and vegetation illustrate the fictional leaf-litter trail.
A restoration landscape illustrates transitions among habitat patches and human-managed land, rather than a surveyed nest margin.
A harbor-side built environment represents the scenario's transport gateway. It does not establish an ant movement route.
The maintained lawn and planted borders illustrate a garden edge in the Mediterranean region.
Exposed ground and low vegetation illustrate an open setting. The photographed slopes are not a measured ant battlefield.
Tree trunks, shade, and understory illustrate the sheltered grove setting. The locality is inland Terrassa, not Marseille.
Woodland-floor cover illustrates the fictional leaf-litter route; this inland Spanish example is not a coastal game nest.
The meeting of vegetation and exposed saline ground illustrates a habitat transition; no ant occurrence is inferred.
The waterfront illustrates human transport infrastructure used as a fictional gateway setting.
A maintained planting boundary illustrates garden-edge surroundings, without identifying an ant nest.
The exposed slope illustrates relatively open surroundings; the game's open-terrain coefficient is not a measurement here.
The tree canopy and sheltered ground illustrate a shaded grove, distinct from the plantation boundary shown for habitat margin.
Close forest-floor cover illustrates the obstacles around the fictional leaf-litter trail, not a measured combat bottleneck.
The documented vegetation boundary illustrates habitat margin. It is not described as intact native forest or an ant frontline.
The vessel and access structures illustrate a human transport edge in the Paraná basin, not a recorded dispersal route.
A planted urban public space illustrates the fictional garden edge; the photographed plaza does not locate the game nest.
The exposed riverbank illustrates open surroundings in the native-range region; no invasion is implied.
River-edge trees and sheltered surroundings illustrate the fictional grove; the photo does not document an ant colony.
The dense understory and fallen woody debris illustrate obstacles around the fictional leaf-litter route. No photographed trail or ant nest is claimed.
Transitions between open water, vegetation, and wooded banks illustrate habitat margin in the Paraná basin.
